title: How to Connect Blink to Claude: Build and Ship Apps from a Chat
summary: Add Blink to Claude or ChatGPT with one URL. Your assistant gets 37 tools — list projects, read logs, query the database, drive the Blink agent, publish to production, restore versions.
body_markdown:
## What you can ask for


Thirty-seven tools, but you never name them. You describe the outcome and Claude picks.


**Look around.**


> "What Blink projects do I have, and which ones are live?"


**Read the code.**


> "Show me how auth is wired in my invoicing app."


**Query the data.**


> "How many users signed up in the last week? Just count them, don't change anything."


Reads are read-only by construction — the query tool accepts a single` SELECT` ,` WITH` ,` EXPLAIN` , or` PRAGMA` and rejects everything else, so an exploratory question can't become an accidental write.


**Debug production.**


> "The checkout page is throwing something. Pull the backend logs from the last hour and tell me what's failing."


**Build.**


> "Add a dark mode toggle to the settings page."


This one is worth understanding, because it is not what most connectors do.


## Claude doesn't edit your files — it briefs an agent that does


There is no write-file tool. When you ask for a change, Claude sends a prompt to the **Blink agent** , the same agent that runs in the chat on blink.new. That agent plans the change, edits the code, checks its own work, and saves a version.


Two AI systems editing one codebase is a recipe for lost work. One owns the files; the other describes what it wants. You get Claude's reasoning about your product and Blink's verified execution on the code, without a merge conflict between them.


A useful consequence: the agent will stop and ask when your request is ambiguous. Claude surfaces the question in chat, you answer in the same sentence you were already writing, and the build resumes.


**Ship it.**


> "Publish it to production."


First publish activates hosting and gives you a live URL on a global CDN with SSL. Later publishes rebuild the live site.


**Undo it.**


> "That broke the nav. Show me what changed since the last version and restore the good one."


Every Blink turn saves a version. Claude can diff two of them and restore either — so an experiment is genuinely cheap.


## Permissions, and what the connector can't do


You approve a specific set of permissions on the consent screen, and Blink never grants more than your role in that workspace allows. A **viewer** can only ever grant read-only access, no matter what the client asks for.


Permission Covers


` workspace:read` Workspace details, credits, skills, connector status


` projects:read` Projects, source, versions, database schema and reads, logs


` projects:write` Create and update projects, database writes, publish, versions


` projects:build` Run the Blink agent — this is the one that spends credits


` ai` Image generation through the AI Gateway


Workspace-level destructive actions are not exposed at all. Claude cannot change your billing, delete your workspace, or transfer ownership — those tools don't exist on the connector, so no misunderstanding can reach them.


Everything connected is listed at **Settings → Access Tokens → Connected apps** , with the workspace it can reach and a Revoke button that takes effect on the next call.


## What it costs


Reading is free. Listing projects, reading source, pulling logs, running a` SELECT` , diffing versions — none of it touches your credits.


Two things do: running the Blink agent, because it is a real build turn, and publishing, because hosting is billed monthly from credits. Ask Claude *"how many credits do I have left?"* any time. Publishing for the first time needs a Starter plan or higher; on Free, the tool hands back an upgrade link instead of failing quietly.


## Is this the same as the Blink MCP npm package?


No, and it's worth being precise, because both are called MCP.


Claude connector` @blinkdotnew/mcp`


**Runs** Hosted by Blink Locally, as an npm process


**Setup** One URL, OAuth sign-in` mcp.json` config plus an API key


**For** Projects you build on blink.new Blink Cloud infrastructure for code you write yourself


**Best in** Claude, ChatGPT Cursor, Claude Code, Codex


If you build on blink.new, you want the connector. If you write code in your own editor and want Blink Cloud to provide the database, auth, and hosting, you want the[npm package](https://blink.new/docs/cloud/tools/mcp) . Plenty of people run both.


## Common problems


The URL must be exactly` https://blink.new/mcp` — no trailing slash, no` www` , HTTPS only. If you hand-edited a config file, make sure the transport is` http` (Streamable HTTP), not the older` sse` .


You likely connected as a viewer in that workspace and then asked for something that writes. Check your role under Settings → Members, then disconnect and reconnect so consent runs again with the right permissions.


It is almost always waiting on a question. The Blink agent pauses when a request is ambiguous rather than guessing. Ask Claude to check the build status — it will surface the question, and your answer resumes the turn.


A first publish activates production hosting, which requires Starter or above and draws that tier's monthly credits. Upgrade through the link and ask again. Republishing a site that's already live has no gate.


Connections are bound to one workspace. If the project is in a different one, reconnect and choose that workspace at the consent step.


Access refreshes automatically, so this usually means the grant was revoked — by you, or by a workspace owner. Reconnect from Settings → Connectors.


## Start here


Connect it, then ask for something small and real:


> "Create a new Blink project called expense-tracker, build me a simple expense log with a chart of monthly spend, and publish it."


One sentence in a chat window, and a live URL comes back.


[Set up the connector →](https://blink.new/docs/cloud/tools/claude-connector)
